items.title: GhostBat RAT - RTO/mParivahan-themed Android campaign
items.summary: Multi-stage Android malware impersonating the mParivahan RTO app, spread via WhatsApp and SMS smishing with shortened URLs. Droppers use ZIP manipulation and native packers; a fake UPI payment flow harvests the UPI PIN, and banking SMS is exfiltrated. Some variants also bundle a cryptominer. 40+ distinct samples observed.

sources.title: Cyble - GhostBat RAT: inside the resurgence of RTO-themed Android malware

items.title: RTO Challan fraud - two-stage dropper (jsonserv C2)
items.summary: e-Challan / RTO-themed two-stage dropper. A fake 'update' prompt installs a second APK that hides its icon (INFO category), collects Aadhaar/PAN and full card/UPI details via fake payment screens, and intercepts incoming SMS for OTP harvesting. C2 over HTTP POST to jsonserv domains.

sources.title: CYFIRMA - RTO Challan Fraud: a technical report on APK-based financial and identity theft

items.title: Ahmedabad APK fraud network (Telegram storefront)
items.summary: Ahmedabad Cyber Crime Branch dismantled a network running a Telegram bot that sold, swapped and renewed fraud APKs impersonating SBI KYC/rewards, other banks, RTO services and utilities. One distributor allegedly supplied ~400 fraudsters; linked losses ~Rs 54 lakh. Cash-out via ATM withdrawals left no direct bank trail. No technical IOCs published.

sources.title: ETV Bharat - Gujarat Police bust pan-India APK fraud racket

items.title: Pune fake RTO e-challan APK scam
items.summary: Two Pune residents lost a combined Rs 14+ lakh after installing APK files attached to fake RTO e-challan notices. Pune police advised checking challans only on official government platforms and never installing APKs from SMS/WhatsApp links.

sources.title: The Bridge Chronicle - Two Punekars lost over Rs 14 lakh in fake RTO e-challan APK scam

items.title: Mumbai interstate APK fraud network (~Rs 43 crore, 3,206 cases)
items.summary: Mumbai Cyber Police arrested six members of an interstate syndicate linked to 3,206 complaints on the national portal (~Rs 43 crore). APKs impersonated banks, Mahanagar Gas (MGL) and the RTO; a typical lure warned of a gas disconnection and asked the victim to install an app and pay Rs 10. The apps intercepted OTPs and banking SMS. Forensics found 111 distinct fake APKs; ~8,609 people installed them, and ~1.24 crore SMS were exfiltrated via servers on Google Firebase and Hostinger.

sources.title: Free Press Journal - 6 arrested as Mumbai cyber police bust Rs 43 crore fake APK fraud network (26 Jun 2026)

items.title: APK lure themes in rotation (2026)
items.summary: Reference entry for the social-engineering lures driving APK fraud in India. The same malware is repackaged behind whatever pretext is topical: RTO/traffic e-challan, bank KYC and reward points (SBI and others), gas and electricity bill updates (e.g. Mahanagar Gas), PM-Kisan and PM-Awas Yojana benefit checks, credit-card offers, 'digital arrest' intimidation, and WhatsApp wedding-invite APKs. All lead to an installed APK that reads SMS/OTPs and drains accounts. Police advice is consistent: never install an app from an SMS/WhatsApp link; use only official channels.

items.title: Android banking trojan - MITM + anti-analysis (case study)
items.summary: Hands-on analysis of a sophisticated Android banking trojan spread from a compromised WhatsApp group, using a man-in-the-middle VPN technique and advanced anti-analysis to steal banking credentials. Representative of the higher end of the Android threat targeting Indian users.
